title: Improved Friedgut family
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a Boolean function on $\{−1,1\}^n$ with values in $\{−1,1\}$, and let $\epsilon,\eta\in\mathbb R$. The improved Friedgut family consists of all finite coordinate sets $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that either every coordinate in $S$ is influential for $f$ at the improved Friedgut threshold $\left(\frac{\epsilon}{I(f)}\rho(\eta)^k\right)^{1+\eta}$, or $k<|S|$, where $I(f)$ is the total influence and $\rho(\eta)=\frac{\eta}{2+\eta}$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function $f$ on $\{−1,1\}^n$ with values in $\{−1,1\}$
caveat: The supplied snippet omits the definition of influential coordinates, so the threshold condition can only be identified by its supplied name and role.
